note: Machine-readable form of openspec/changes/align-desktop-project-execution-with-master/execution-contract.md. v1.json keeps describing the read-only remote workbench and is NOT widened by this file: v2 adds execution frames, phases, effects, limits and artifacts as a separate protocol major that a client may declare optional. Python reads it through auth/desktop_contracts_v2.py; the desktop client compiles the same constants in desktop/src/main/project-execution/contract.ts and tests/test_desktop_execution_contract.cjs fails if any of them drifts from this document, so a phase name or a limit can only change in one place. Field names are snake_case; sizes are bytes; times are seconds unless the key says otherwise.

protocol.name: project_execution
protocol.absent_means: the new entry point is unavailable; v1 inspects/materializes stay as they are, and a v2 operation is never downgraded into them

platforms.note: Whether this build's execution end has an accepted launcher for the platform. A platform that is not supported reports platform_unsupported and offers no tools at all -- claiming the file tools while the launcher cannot confine a process would be the more dangerous half-truth.

posix.note: macOS/Linux via the same sandbox path the local worker uses

win32.note: the Windows launcher and probes are not accepted yet; v2 frames are refused with platform_unsupported rather than translated

tools.note: The master tool names a v2 frame may carry. The server proxies the *current* tool view, so the name, its description and its JSON schema stay the master's; only the execution end changes.

posix.bash: sh -c with $VAR expansion and POSIX quoting, as the master bash tool documents

windows.bash: unsupported until the Windows launcher and probes are accepted. Today win32 is not an accepted platform at all, so a bash frame on it is refused by the platform check with unsupported_platform (422), before the tool is even considered. If win32 is ever accepted as a platform, the tool check must still refuse this frame -- feature_unavailable (503), never a translation into POSIX syntax.

frames.note: Frame types added on top of v1's gateway frame_types. A v2 frame always carries protocol_major=2 so a v1-only reader refuses it instead of guessing.

execute_tool.forbidden_note: the project root comes from the main process resolving workspace_id; arguments never name a cwd, a module path or a credential, and the endpoint never accepts a caller-chosen URL or header

execution_result.result_note: the tool's own payload, exactly as the execution end's tool produced it: {status, result, display, ext_data, duration_ms}. A file tool's answer travels here; stdout/stderr/exit_code describe a script. The server hands it to the model unedited, so both modes return one shape.

phases.note: The visible phase is derived from the existing server command state plus cancel_requested; the states themselves are v1's command states and are not renamed.

effects.note: What a terminal result may claim about the project directory. A stopped process never promises a rollback.

error_codes.note: Only codes v2 adds. v1's error_codes stay the single source for the codes they already define; auth/desktop_contracts_v2.status_for() merges the two and refuses a code that appears in both with different statuses.

limits.note: v2 additions. Keys listed in reuse_v1 are read from v1.json instead of being restated here, so the two documents cannot disagree.
limits.advisory_note: Declared budgets the current launcher does NOT enforce. They stay in this document as the intended bound, but they are withheld from the capability block's advertised `limits`: a client reads that block as "these are the caps that will be applied", and this module's rule is the same one that makes a Windows build report no script tool -- never advertise an enforcement the launcher does not have. Moving a key out of `advisory` requires the enforcement to land first (A17's resource-limit dimension, currently open).

artifact.note: What a local result references. The client's absolute paths never enter the server artifact; relative_path is inside the authorised workspace.
artifact.source_version_note: derived from file identity, size and mtime (plus a digest when needed), never from the display name

start_permit.note: Short-lived, single-use proof that the server still allows this command to start. Credentials never travel into the worker.

journal.note: The local start journal. Written before the worker can touch the project, so a crash leaves evidence instead of an ambiguous silence.
journal.started_without_completed_note: neither 'not executed' nor 'succeeded' may be inferred; only the original journal and files may be inspected

broker.note: Narrow endpoints the desktop main process calls before and during an execution. They reuse the existing native-only authentication, access service, command records and audit. No generic server URL, no caller-chosen auth header, no arbitrary module path.

skill_package.note: The one broker read that returns bytes. A device that was told to run a pinned skill version but does not hold it asks for exactly that version, naming the command it was told to run and the digest it was given; the server answers only when the pair is in the set that command was authorized with. The bytes come from the server's own skill directory after a live authorization check, and the digest is recomputed there, so what is shipped is what the digest covers.

capability.note: The optional project_execution block a v2 client reads from meta/hello. It reports only limits that are actually enforced; tests and probes decide what may be claimed, not this file alone.

meta_additions.note: Keys a v2 build adds to the existing meta envelope. The v1 required keys and forbidden keys are unchanged, and the payload stays inside the v1 byte cap.
